startup.name: Vantel
startup.one_liner: AI Platform for Commercial Insurance Brokerages
startup.description: An AI operating system for commercial insurance brokerages, built by a five person team in Stockholm. Brokerages pay a software subscription to automate documents, submissions and CRM work. Tags are Documents, Insurance and CRM. Forecast as of 2025-01-06, window to 2026-11-17 (about 22 months).

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is in the Winter 2025 batch, so this is shown for completeness. Start from the roughly 1 percent prior for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent range in yc_acceptance.md). Adjust up for a five person team, a defined buyer and a sector where YC has funded many insurance workflow companies, and keep it near 2 percent because no traction is stated.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because AI for insurance brokers is a crowded theme with several funded entrants, and a Stockholm team with no stated broker customers or revenue gives little proof that brokers will switch from their agency management system. The partners would also ask why this team beats funded rivals such as Herald and the mulligan style startups already in earlier batches.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --tag Insurance gave seed 50% / 54% / 57% (lower / known / upper, n=42, cond 54%); same command with --industry Fintech gave 54% / 61% / 65% (n=219). Window rule: knowledge/tables/time_to_milestones.csv shows 2022+ months to seed p25 3, p50 6, p75 14.2, so about 85 percent of ever reachers have raised by 22 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Ever anchor about 0.54 times 0.85 for the 22 month window gives 0.46. Held at 0.45 with no lift for team size or sector, per the winners test rule that such lifts did not separate companies. Within 1.25 times of the anchor, and the odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: A small post YC round of about $1M to $3M from angels and a micro fund, the most common outcome when a team has early pilots but no repeatable sales motion. It is the largest band because the 2022 and later seed table (p25 $2.0M, median $3.5M) mixes in YC deal sized checks.
A conventional institutional seed of $3M to $6M led by a seed fund, matching the 2022 and later table median of $3.5M and the p75 of $5.2M for the cohort.

A $6M to $12M seed, which happens when a lead fund prices on market heat. Among confirmed 2026 raises above $1M the median was $6.0M, but press covers large rounds more, so this band is kept at a minority.
An upside seed above $12M, reached only if the company shows unusual early revenue or a top fund competes for it; rare in the YC data and kept small.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window is 22 months (2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17); seed means an outside round above about $1M. The most likely miss is a team that stays on the YC deal plus angels because broker pilots stay unpaid or small. Commercial brokerages buy slowly and lean on Applied Epic or Vertafore, and investors see rivals such as Mulligan and Herald, so a Stockholm team without US logos can fail to convince a lead. Infer and Lucite show the small round path.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --tag Insurance gave series_a 19% / 21% / 26% with cond 38% (n=21); --industry Fintech gave cond 24% (n=119). Time rule: 2022+ months to series A p25 19.4, p50 28, so under a third of ever reachers close an A inside 22 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Ever conditional of 0.24 to 0.38 is scaled by about 0.35 for the 22 month window, then rounded up to 0.10. That is more than 2x below the anchor only because the window cuts off most Series A closings, which arrive at a median of 28 months.

bands.rationale: A thin or bridge style Series A of $6M to $10M, common when growth is real but revenue is still small; below the 2022 and later p25 of $11M, so it stands for the soft band.
The central Series A of $10M to $18M, bracketing the 2022 and later median of $15M and p25 to p75 of $11M to $21M.
A larger A of $18M to $30M that top funds lead when growth looks category defining; current market data shows A deal sizes near $17M to $20M.
An upside A above $30M, seen only for a few AI companies with very fast revenue; rare and kept at a small share.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside the window needs paid broker revenue that is already growing fast, and a European based seed stage company rarely gets there in under two years. Investors will compare against Fair Square, which needed about two years after YC to raise its $15M A, and against better funded US rivals. Missing recurring revenue or retention data is the usual reason an A does not come.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --tag Insurance gave series_b cond 25% (n=8); --industry B2B gave cond 21% (n=123). These are long run (not window) numbers and 2022+ batches are right censored.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Within 0.75 to 1.0 times the anchor. This step is the long run chance beyond the forecast window, not a window figure.

bands.rationale: A smaller or flat Series B of $15M to $30M, typical when the A cohort slows; includes down or extension rounds.
The central Series B of $30M to $50M, matching the 2022 and later median of $40M with p25 to p75 of $27M to $55M.
A growth B of $50M to $80M for companies with clear scaled revenue.
An upside B above $80M for category leaders, rare among YC companies.

ladder.why_it_fails: By Series B a brokerage software company has to show net revenue retention and a path past a few hundred brokerage customers. Insurance workflow vendors tend to plateau because brokerages are a bounded set of buyers and agency management vendors can bundle similar AI features. Many insurance tag companies stall after an A, so the miss is usually growth too slow to justify a $30M plus round.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --tag Insurance gave series_c cond 0% (n=2); --industry B2B gave cond 19% (n=26). Older cohorts reach 36 to 43 percent, so 0.25 is a blend.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Within 1.25 times the B2B anchor; the Insurance cohort has too few cases to use and older eras ran higher.

bands.rationale: A modest later round of $30M to $60M, including down rounds and structured deals.
The central round of $60M to $120M, bracketing the 2022 and later series C median of $74M.
A large growth round of $120M to $250M for a clear leader.
A mega round above $250M, which only a handful of YC companies have reached.

ladder.why_it_fails: A growth round past B requires becoming the system of record or a distribution layer for brokerages. If the product stays an add on to Applied Epic or Vertafore, the company is acquired or flattens first, as the many insurance tool exits suggest. Capital would also be needed to expand beyond the Nordics into US commercial lines, a slow and licence heavy path.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely stall: the product becomes a feature of broker platforms or a point tool, and the team is acqui-hired or runs out of runway. Insurance tag cohorts show about 10 percent acquired and 5 to 12 percent shut down, but a larger share simply stall at small revenue. Reaching $100M plus needs system of record status in a market where Applied and Vertafore are entrenched.

analogs.relevance: Insurance brokerage startup from YC W20 that later sold AI tools to carriers
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $15M Series A in 2022 about two years after its batch, then pivoted toward AI voice tools for carriers in 2024; shows a slow, small insurance A path.

analogs.relevance: Operating system for insurance agencies, same buyer segment (YC S21)
analogs.outcome_summary: Took the $125K YC seed in 2021, pivoted to insurance voice AI around 2023 and has no verified institutional round in the record, a small round or no round path.

analogs.relevance: AI automation for insurance brokerages, document workflows (as Pyq, W23)
analogs.outcome_summary: Began as a document comparison tool, found its niche with brokers pulling it into quoting; no priced round in the record, showing that broker AI can be sold but slowly.

analogs.relevance: Tools for insurance brokers and advisors (W24)
analogs.outcome_summary: Four person team that reportedly raised about $500K, the YC deal sized outcome rather than an institutional seed.

analogs.relevance: Broker network software run by repeat founders (S22)
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $1.7M pre-seed then about $5M seed within a year, showing that a strong team in a broker market can raise a seed fast.

killers.risk: Incumbent agency management systems and carriers bundle AI document and submission features
killers.evidence: Applied Epic and Vertafore own the broker workflow and data, and Herald raised a $12M Series A in October 2024 with Lightspeed to connect brokers and carriers.
killers.mitigation: Pick one workflow such as submission intake where the incumbents are weakest and integrate with them instead of replacing them.

killers.risk: No repeatable paid pilots, so seed investors see only a services style engagement
killers.evidence: Brokerages buy slowly and pilots are often free; Infer and Lucite show small YC deal sized outcomes in the same buyer segment.
killers.mitigation: Charge from the first pilot and report weekly active brokers and annual contract value in the seed deck.

killers.risk: A Stockholm team with a mostly US commercial lines market lacks licences, references and local network
killers.evidence: The team is based in Sweden while the largest commercial brokerage spend is in the US, and a 22 month window gives limited time to build US references.
killers.mitigation: Move two founders to a US hub during the batch and win one named top 100 brokerage as a design partner.

competition_now.name: Herald
competition_now.what: Commercial insurance API and AI layer between brokers and carriers
competition_now.traction: $12M Series A in October 2024 led by Lightspeed; works with 8 of the top 25 brokerages by its own claim

competition_now.name: Applied Systems (Applied Epic)
competition_now.what: Incumbent broker management system with a large installed base
competition_now.traction: Default system of record for many brokerages

competition_now.name: Vertafore
competition_now.what: Incumbent agency and broker software suite
competition_now.traction: Long established vendor with carrier relationships

technical_complexity.rationale: Document extraction, submission parsing and CRM sync are buildable by five people in three months on current language models, but quality on messy ACORD forms and integration with agency systems are the hard parts. Hard parts are solvable by a small team and become a mild moat once integrations exist.

who: Herald and other funded insurtech startups
takeover_risk.rationale: A funded rival or an incumbent could ship comparable document automation within about a year and already owns distribution. Incentive is high because AI features defend renewals, but incumbents are slow to ship, so the risk is medium.

evidence.claim: Funded rivals show investors and brokers pay for AI in commercial brokerage workflows; Herald closed a $12M Series A in October 2024 with brokers as users.
Commercial brokerage work is manual, with submissions and policy comparison relying on people (market commentary, mid 2025 and later, used only as a directional signal).

roadmap.goal: Show brokers will pay, not just try
actions: Sign 3 brokerages to paid pilots before demo day
Record hours saved per submission from real broker files
roadmap.proof: 3 paying brokerages and a measured time saving per submission

roadmap.goal: Turn pilots into repeatable ARR that a lead can underwrite
actions: Hire a US based sales lead and a US customer reference
Integrate with Applied Epic or Vertafore so deployment takes days
roadmap.proof: At least $15K to $25K monthly recurring revenue across 10 or more brokerages

roadmap.goal: Prove expansion across brokerage staff and lines
actions: Add a second workflow such as renewals or certificates
Reach 2x net revenue retention in the first cohort
roadmap.proof: $1M ARR and net revenue retention above 110 percent

pros.point: Clear buyer and painful manual workflow
pros.evidence: Commercial brokerage submissions and documents are manual and brokers are a defined, reachable buyer set.

pros.point: Active investor interest in the category
pros.evidence: Herald closed a $12M Series A in October 2024 for commercial broker infrastructure.

brand.name: Vantel
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Vantel" --era 2022+ gave kind invented_or_proper, 6 characters, 2 syllables, no suffix or digits.
strengths: Short, pronounceable and easy to spell
Invented word with no descriptor to date it
weaknesses: Sounds like several existing fintech names
brand.rationale: A short invented name is the most common pattern among YC winners such as Stripe or Brex and neither helps nor hurts; the name does not signal insurance, so the product must carry the message. A neutral effect, so it does not move the ladder.

narrative.headline: A plausible but undifferentiated AI tool for insurance brokers, likely to reach a small seed within 22 months and an A only slowly.
narrative.general_summary: Vantel sells AI automation to commercial insurance brokerages from Stockholm with five people. The category has real pain and funded competitors, so investor interest is likely but not a ranking advantage. In a 22 month window the cohort anchor puts a seed above $1M near 45 percent, and a Series A inside the window is unlikely because the median A arrives about 28 months after the batch. The main risk is bundling by Applied and Vertafore plus slow broker sales cycles. Odds here do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Forecast made blind from the input file only; the window runs 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17, about 22 months.
Seed means an outside round above about $1M; the YC deal alone does not count.
Seed and Series A odds are for the window; Series B and C odds are long run conditional rates.
Cohort rates for Insurance (n=42) and Fintech are 2022 to 2024 batches and right censored; funding data is incomplete so known-only rates read low.
Web search covered the market only; several results were dated after the as_of date and were ignored.
